messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

The user wants to find public libraries in three cities with specific facilities. We need to call the function for each city with the appropriate facilities. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby takes location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated strings: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

We need to pass an array for facilities? The type says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That seems ambiguous: maybe facilities can be a string or an array of strings? The example says "Cafe"[] meaning array of "Cafe"? Actually the type is union of string or array of "Cafe"? Might be a mistake. But we can pass an array of strings: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] etc. For the first request: reading room and fiction. So call with location: "New York, NY" and facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]. For second: Wi-Fi and children section. So location: "Los Angeles, CA" and facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]. Third: cafe and reading room. So location: "Chicago, IL" and facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

We need to call the function three times. The function returns any. We need to output the results. We'll call the function for each city.
